喀斯特地貌的形成与识别: Formation and Recognition of Karst Landforms
可溶岩 + 水 → 溶沟 → 洼地 → 峰丛峰林 → 孤峰残丘 · 地下溶洞: Soluble rock + water → solution grooves → depressions → peak clusters and peak forests → isolated peaks and residual hills · underground caves
徐霞客写的「峭峰离立，分行竞颖」——这些像从地里长出来的尖峰，是怎么一块岩层变出: Xu Xiake wrote of "sheer peaks standing apart, rising in rows as if vying with each other". How did these spikes that seem to grow out of the ground come from a single rock layer?
可溶性岩石的物质溶于水被带走、或重新沉淀: Material in soluble rock dissolves in water and is carried away, or is redeposited
溶沟：长条形 / 网格状，地面高低不平: Solution grooves: long strips or a grid, leaving the ground uneven
溶沟发展成洼地；底部平坦的坝子是农耕区: Grooves grow into depressions; flat-floored bazi basins are farmland
洼地边缘残留岩体：峰丛 → 峰林 → 孤峰 → 残丘: Rock left at depression edges: peak cluster → peak forest → isolated peak → residual hill
地下以溶洞为主；洞顶石钟乳向下、洞底石笋向上，接上成石柱: Underground it is mostly caves; stalactites grow down from the roof and stalagmites up from the floor, joining into columns
溶沟到洼地（坝子）这一段地表: The surface stretch from solution grooves to depressions (bazi)
岩块下半的洞腔与洞内堆积（石钟乳 / 石笋）: The cave in the lower half of the block and its deposits (stalactites / stalagmites)
什么样的岩石能被水「溶」出地貌？: What kind of rock can water "dissolve" into landforms?
拖动视角绕岩块看一圈：岩层的层理、裂隙，和上方落下的雨: Drag the view around the block: the rock's bedding, its fractures and the rain falling from above
可溶岩块（层理 + 裂隙）+ 降雨；溶蚀速率 20.0 mm/ka（年降水 14: Soluble rock block (bedding + fractures) + rainfall; dissolution rate 20.0 mm/ka (annual rainfall 1400 mm, mean annual temperature 18 ℃); reaching the solution groove stage takes 200,000 years
广西 · 贵州 · 云南最典型: Most typical in Guangxi · Guizhou · Yunnan
组成地壳的岩石有一部分是可溶性岩石，如石灰岩。: Some of the rocks making up the crust are soluble, such as limestone.
在适当条件下，这类岩石的物质溶于水并被带走，或重新沉淀。: Under suitable conditions, material in such rocks dissolves in water and is carried away, or is redeposited.
地表和地下因此形成形态各异的地貌，统称喀斯特地貌；我国广西、贵州、云南最典型。: This creates varied landforms on the surface and underground, together called karst landforms; in China they are most typical in Guangxi, Guizhou and Yunnan.
去掉这一步：学生会把喀斯特说成风蚀或流水搬运堆积。: Skip this step and students may describe karst as wind erosion or deposition by running water.
易错：把喀斯特地貌的成因说成「风蚀」或「流水搬运堆积」——是物质溶于水被带走或重: Common mistake: giving the cause of karst as "wind erosion" or "transport and deposition by running water"; it is material dissolving in water and being carried away or redeposited.
可溶性岩石（如石灰岩）的物质溶于水并被带走、或重新沉淀，在地表和地下形成形态各异: Material in soluble rock (such as limestone) dissolves in water and is carried away, or is redeposited, forming varied landforms on the surface and underground, together called karst landforms.
facts A2.1（p.66）、A5 #1/#2；B2.1 ②③、B3 第 1: facts A2.1 (p.66), A5 #1/#2; B2.1 ②③, B3 row 1
溶沟怎么变大成洼地？: How do solution grooves grow into depressions?
把「演化阶段」从溶沟拖到洼地：看地表从浅浅的沟槽变成一块宽凹地: Drag "evolution stage" from solution grooves to depressions: the surface changes from shallow channels into a broad hollow
地表起伏 1 → 6 m；累积溶蚀深度 4 → 14 m；残余岩体占比 100: Surface relief 1 → 6 m; cumulative dissolution depth 4 → 14 m; remaining rock share 100 % → 85 %; time to reach 200,000 → 700,000 years
坝子是洼地的地方称呼: Bazi is the local name for a depression
溶沟呈长条形或网格状，地面高低不平、崎岖难行。: Solution grooves form long strips or a grid, leaving the ground uneven and hard to cross.
溶沟进一步发展，可形成面积较大的洼地。: As grooves develop further, they can form larger depressions.
底部平坦的洼地在云南、贵州叫坝子，是当地重要的农耕区——坝子是洼地的地方称呼，不: Flat-floored depressions in Yunnan and Guizhou are called bazi and are important farmland; bazi is the local name for a depression, not another landform type.
去掉这一步：「坝子」会被当成一种地貌类型。: Skip this step and "bazi" may be taken as a landform type.
易错：把「坝子」当成地貌类型——它是洼地在云南、贵州等地的称呼。: Common mistake: treating "bazi" as a landform type; it is what depressions are called in Yunnan, Guizhou and nearby.
溶沟进一步发展可形成面积较大的洼地；底部平坦的洼地被当地人称为坝子，是重要的农耕: Solution grooves can develop into larger depressions; flat-floored depressions are called bazi by local people and are important farmland.
洼地边缘为什么立起一座座尖峰？: Why do spikes rise one after another around the edges of a depression?
把阶段从洼地拖到峰林，盯住岩块正面的上沿：峰丛是一排尖峰连在一道墙上，峰林是尖峰: Drag the stage from depression to peak forest, watching the top edge of the block's front: a peak cluster is a row of spikes joined in one wall, while a peak forest has spikes cut down to the plain and standing apart
地表起伏 6 → 24 → 42 m（峰值在峰林）；残余岩体占比 85 % →: Surface relief 6 → 24 → 42 m (peak at the peak forest); remaining rock share 85 % → 65 % → 45 %; cumulative dissolution depth 14 → 32 → 58 m
峰丛基座相连 · 峰林彼此分立: Peak cluster bases joined · peak forest standing apart
起伏峰值在峰林（示意）: Relief peaks at the peak forest (illustrative)
洼地边缘残留的岩体常呈锥状耸立，构成峰丛、峰林。: Rock left at the edges of depressions often rises as upright cones, forming peak clusters and peak forests.
识别要点：峰丛的锥峰下部连成一整块基座，峰林的锥峰彼此分开。: Key to recognition: the cones of a peak cluster are joined into one base below, while those of a peak forest stand apart.
起伏度在这里到峰值（42 m）：地面被切得最碎。: Relief reaches its maximum here (42 m): the ground is most broken up.
去掉这一步：峰丛与峰林分不清——这是本课最高频的错。: Skip this step and peak clusters and peak forests get confused, the most frequent mistake in this lesson.
易错：把峰丛与峰林颠倒或分不清——峰丛基座相连、峰林彼此分立，峰丛在峰林之前。: Common mistake: swapping or confusing peak clusters and peak forests. Peak clusters have joined bases, peak forests stand apart, and the cluster comes before the forest.
洼地边缘残留的岩体呈锥状耸立，构成峰丛、峰林；峰丛的锥峰下部连成基座，峰林彼此分: Rock left at depression edges rises as upright cones, forming peak clusters and peak forests; cluster cones join into a base below, forest cones stand apart, and relief is greatest at the peak forest stage.
峰林再溶下去会剩什么？: If the peak forest keeps dissolving, what is left?
把阶段从峰林拖到残丘：看锥峰越来越少、基座消失、最后只剩低矮岩块: Drag the stage from peak forest to residual hill: the cones grow fewer, the base disappears, and finally only low rock blocks remain
地表起伏 42 → 30 → 12 m（先升后降，这一段在降）；残余岩体占比 4: Surface relief 42 → 30 → 12 m (rising then falling; this stretch is falling); remaining rock share 45 % → 25 % → 10 %; cumulative dissolution depth 58 → 88 → 120 m
峰林 → 孤峰 → 残丘: Peak forest → isolated peak → residual hill
起伏在峰林之后反而降下来: Relief actually falls after the peak forest
峰林可演变为孤峰，以至残丘：基座消失、只剩一两座孤立岩峰，最后是低矮零星岩块。: A peak forest can evolve into isolated peaks and finally residual hills: the base disappears, leaving one or two isolated peaks, and at last low, scattered rock blocks.
起伏度先升后降（42 → 30 → 12 m），残余岩体从 45 % 降到 10: Relief rises then falls (42 → 30 → 12 m), and the remaining rock share falls from 45 % to 10 %.
顺序不能颠倒：孤峰不是演变的第一步。: The order cannot be reversed: an isolated peak is not the first step of the evolution.
去掉这一步：学生把孤峰当成演变的起点。: Skip this step and students take the isolated peak as the starting point.
易错：把孤峰说成演变的第一步；把「越往后起伏越大」当规律。: Common mistake: calling the isolated peak the first step; treating "the later, the greater the relief" as a rule.
峰林可演变为孤峰、以至残丘：基座消失、岩体越来越少、越来越低；起伏度在峰林之后反: A peak forest can evolve into isolated peaks and then residual hills: the base disappears and the rock gets less and lower; relief actually falls after the peak forest.
同样的岩石，为什么有的地方蚀得快？: With the same rock, why does it dissolve faster in some places?
把「年降水量」从 1400 拖到 600 mm：看溶蚀变慢、到达同一阶段要多等多: Drag "annual rainfall" from 1400 to 600 mm: dissolution slows, and see how much longer it takes to reach the same stage
Dissolution rate 20.0 → 8.6 mm/ka; reaching the peak forest takes 2.9 → 6.767 million years; at the comparison extreme (rainfall 2400 + mean temperature 25 ℃) the rate is 39.1 mm/ka and the time 1.484 million years
「溶于水」要有水、也要有热量：降水多、温度高，溶蚀就快。: "Dissolving in water" needs water and also heat: more rain and higher temperature mean faster dissolution.
同一个峰林阶段，降水 1400 mm 要 290.0 万年，降到 600 mm: For the same peak forest stage, 1400 mm of rain takes 2.9 million years, while 600 mm takes 6.767 million years.
所以喀斯特在我国西南发育得好——水热条件都够。: That is why karst is well developed in southwest China: there is enough water and heat.
去掉这一步：学生会以为喀斯特哪里都能长成峰林。: Skip this step and students think karst can grow into peak forests anywhere.
常考：降水多、气温高 → 溶蚀快；反之到达同一阶段需要更久。: Common exam point: more rain and higher temperature → faster dissolution; otherwise the same stage takes longer to reach.
喀斯特发育要在「适当条件」下：水多、温度高，溶蚀快，到达同一阶段的时间短。: Karst develops "under suitable conditions": with plenty of water and high temperature, dissolution is fast and the same stage is reached sooner.
facts A2.1「在适当条件下」（p.66）；B2.1 ②③、B3 第 4: facts A2.1 "under suitable conditions" (p.66); B2.1 ②③, B3 rows 4 / 5, B4 D6/D7
洞里那些「石头」往哪个方向长？: Which way do the "stones" in the cave grow?
把「洞内堆积时间」拖到 20.0 万年：盯住石钟乳的顶端往下走、石笋的顶端往上走: Drag "cave deposition time" to 200,000 years: watch the stalactite tip move down and the stalagmite tip move up
石钟乳与石笋各长到 10.0 m（洞高 12 m）；石钟乳顶端由 12 → 2: Stalactite and stalagmite each grow to 10.0 m (cave height 12 m); the stalactite tip goes from 12 → 2 m (downward), the stalagmite tip from 0 → 10 m (upward); joining into a column takes 120,000 years, so by 200,000 years a column has formed
接上成石柱（12 m 的洞要 12.0 万年）: Joined into a column (a 12 m cave takes 120,000 years)
地下喀斯特地貌以溶洞为主；溶洞长数米到数百千米，常常呈层状分布。: Underground karst is mainly caves; caves range from a few meters to hundreds of kilometers long and are often layered.
洞顶常见向下发育的石钟乳、石幔或石帘；洞底常见向上发育的石笋。: The roof often has stalactites, flowstone drapes or curtains growing down; the floor often has stalagmites growing up.
两者接上就是石柱：12 m 高的洞要 12.0 万年。: When the two join they form a column: a 12 m high cave takes 120,000 years.
去掉这一步：石钟乳与石笋的方向极易说反，也没有「洞高决定时间」这条量。: Skip this step and the directions of stalactites and stalagmites are easily swapped, with no sense that "cave height sets the time".
易错：把石钟乳和石笋的方向说反——洞顶向下、洞底向上；也易错在说成「水冲下来的泥: Common mistake: swapping the directions of stalactites and stalagmites (roof downward, floor upward); another is saying they are "mud and sand washed down by water".
溶洞顶部向下发育石钟乳、石幔或石帘，底部向上发育石笋，两者连接起来形成石柱；洞越: Stalactites, drapes or curtains grow down from the cave roof and stalagmites up from the floor, joining to form columns; the higher the cave, the longer they take to join.
考核：把地表做到起伏最大的那一阶段，并让石钟乳与石笋刚好接上: Check: bring the surface to the stage of greatest relief, and make the stalactite and stalagmite just join
两件事一起做：地表找到起伏最大的阶段；洞里让石钟乳与石笋接上（洞高 12 m）: Do two things together: find the stage of greatest relief on the surface; in the cave, make the stalactite and stalagmite join (cave height 12 m)
达标的一组：阶段＝峰林（起伏 42 m、残余岩体 45 %）、洞内堆积 12.0: One passing setting: stage = peak forest (relief 42 m, remaining rock 45 %), cave deposition 120,000 years → stalactite and stalagmite 6.0 m each, both tips at the 6 m half-height, column formed
峰林 + 石钟乳与石笋相接: Peak forest + stalactite and stalagmite joined
起伏最大的阶段是峰林，不是最后一步（残丘又平下去了）。: The stage of greatest relief is the peak forest, not the last step (residual hills flatten out again).
洞里「接上」只需要时间够：洞越高，接上要越久。: "Joining" in the cave only needs enough time: the higher the cave, the longer it takes.
地表与地下是两条独立的线，各按各的控件走。: The surface and the underground are two independent lines, each following its own control.
去掉这一步：学生把「越往后越起伏」当规律，也把「越往后越快成柱」当规律。: Skip this step and students take "the later, the more relief" and "the later, the faster a column forms" as rules.
考核：能说出「起伏峰值在峰林」与「成柱时间由洞高决定」。: Check: be able to say "relief peaks at the peak forest" and "the time to form a column is set by the cave height".
起伏最大的阶段是峰林；石钟乳与石笋接上只需要时间够，洞越高要等越久。: The stage of greatest relief is the peak forest; stalactites and stalagmites join once there has been enough time, and the higher the cave, the longer the wait.
facts B2.1 ①④、B3 第 2 / 10 行、B4 D2/D5: facts B2.1 ①④, B3 rows 2 / 10, B4 D2/D5

起伏最大的不是最后那一步；洞的净高越大，接上要越久: The greatest relief is not at the last step; the taller the cave, the longer joining takes
流水搬运堆积: Transport and deposition by running water

是一种独立的地貌类型: It is an independent landform type
是洼地在云南、贵州等地的称呼: It is what depressions are called in Yunnan, Guizhou and nearby
是峰林的一种: It is a kind of peak forest

④ 峰丛峰林: ④ Peak clusters and peak forests
峰丛与峰林的识别依据是: Peak clusters and peak forests are told apart by
峰丛基座相连、峰林彼此分立: Peak clusters have joined bases, peak forests stand apart
峰丛比峰林矮: Peak clusters are lower than peak forests
峰林基座相连、峰丛分立: Peak forests have joined bases, peak clusters stand apart
地表喀斯特的演变顺序是: The evolution order of surface karst is
孤峰 → 峰林 → 溶沟 → 洼地: Isolated peak → peak forest → solution grooves → depression
溶沟 → 洼地 → 峰丛、峰林 → 孤峰 → 残丘: Solution grooves → depression → peak cluster, peak forest → isolated peak → residual hill
残丘 → 孤峰 → 峰丛 → 溶沟: Residual hill → isolated peak → peak cluster → solution grooves
洼地 → 溶沟 → 孤峰 → 峰林: Depression → solution grooves → isolated peak → peak forest
A2.2 #1–#4 逐字连读（p.67）。: A2.2 #1–#4 read together word for word (p.67).
关于溶洞，正确的是: Which statement about caves is correct?
都很小，只有几米: They are all small, only a few meters
长数米到数百千米，常常呈层状分布: They range from a few meters to hundreds of kilometers long and are often layered
都在地表: They are all on the surface
石钟乳与石笋的发育方向是: The growth directions of stalactites and stalagmites are
石钟乳在洞顶向下、石笋在洞底向上: Stalactites downward from the roof, stalagmites upward from the floor
石钟乳和石笋连接起来形成的: Formed when a stalactite and a stalagmite join
洞顶崩落的石块: Rock fallen from the cave roof
水流冲来的泥沙堆积: Mud and sand washed in by water
旋转、缩放岩块: Rotate and zoom the rock block
看懂一块可溶岩块怎么被水溶出六个阶段的地表形态，以及洞里那些「石头」往哪个方向长: See how water dissolves a soluble rock block through six surface stages, and which way the "stones" in the cave grow.
示意声明：阶段顺序与形态照教材 p.67 与图 4.2；起伏度、残余岩体占比、累: Illustrative note: stage order and shapes follow textbook p.67 and Fig. 4.2; relief, remaining rock share, cumulative dissolution depth, dissolution rate and time are lesson illustrations (time in units of 10,000 years); the block is exaggerated about 5 times vertically, the dashed line = the original surface, and the thickness of grooves and cave deposits is illustrative; the layered caves are not used to judge which is older.
峰丛：锥峰下部连成基座: Peak cluster: cones joined into a base below
